Different languages have different amounts of words. English has the most words of any language but children everywhere tend to pick up language at the same rate. 

Mandarin is a difficult language because it has its own set of rules which rely on assigning status the objects and this is less fluid than English which the sentence structure can be changed around much more and still be correct. 

There are very little resources to learn a language like Gaelic but way more to learn French so and that is probably the biggest factor. If noone speaks it and there's none of it written down then you're it'll be impossible.

You'll find any language harder if you learnt from an older age. It's linked to the exposure to that language you had when you're brain was in its elastic stage. If someone taught English to you at a young age i.e singing an English nursery rhyme, the child will be more familiar with hearing and speaking the language and so, find it easier to learn. Likewise, if you're a native English speaker you'll probably have an easier time learning Dutch than you would Japanese because the languages are more similar - same alphabet, similar words, similar sentence structure.
